result.title: Permission to Retry: A Study of Authorization and Recovery in AI Agent Workflows
result.summary: A durable agent can resume a consequential action while its authority changes and the action's external outcome remains uncertain. We study execution-time reliability of tool-using AI agents, isolating recovery decisions from language-model behavior. Checkpoint state, permission to dispatch, evidence of an external effect and permission to reconcile are distinct obligations. We present a finite conformance study that checks these obligations through histories scored against a provider effect ledger hidden from the recovering application. A prospectively frozen campaign executes 336 histories on native LangGraph and Temporal hosts, crossing 14 schedules, three provider contracts and four matched application policies. All 168 paired host cells have identical checked outcomes. Per host, retained-ledger reconciliation passes all 42 histories: 21 checked completions, 15 denials and six unknown outcomes with reservations retained. Cached retry, revalidation before retry and stable-key retry pass 30, 36 and 31 histories respectively. A separate 16-case component study of InfinityOS, an enterprise AI platform developed by Arya.ai, exercises exported authority, worker, recovery and settlement code over repository fakes. The results isolate the roles of current authority, provider contracts and retained observations in recovery, with safety, completion and unresolved obligations reported separately for the declared application profile.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究工具型 AI agent 的执行期可靠性，把检查点状态、派发许可、外部效果证据与对账许可拆为不同义务，并在 LangGraph 与 Temporal 上以 336 条历史做有限一致性检验，比较多种重试策略的通过情况。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「状态留存—效果证据—是否重试/对账」的义务划分，可能为 LVR 中重新观察视觉证据、停止与重试决策提供概念框架，可供核查；但论文本身不涉及视觉推理或 latent 状态。
